question: Why do neural networks usually have weights and biases in every layer?
direct_answer: Because each layer needs its own learnable transformation.
expanded_answer: Each layer performs a different linear transformation of its inputs before applying an activation. Separate weights and biases let each layer learn a different representation, so the network can build more complex behavior step by step.
key_points: Each layer has its own parameters
common_wrong_ideas: All layers share the same weights by default
Only the first layer needs parameters
Biases are unnecessary once there are multiple layers
